protections: Upload-folder containment: CamaleonCmsUploader.valid_folder_path? rejects '..', absolute paths and '://' in settings[:folder]; it is called only from upload_file (app/uploaders/camaleon_cms_uploader.rb:128-132; app/helpers/camaleon_cms/uploader_helper.rb:62).

Media-key normalization: String#cama_fix_media_key rewrites '../' and './', collapses repeated slashes and forces a leading '/'; it is applied to S3 object keys in file_parse/add_file/add_folder/delete_folder/delete_file and to media DB lookups (lib/ext/string.rb:98-103; app/uploaders/camaleon_cms_aws_uploader.rb:49,89,109,118,126; app/models/camaleon_cms/media.rb:27).
Filename sanitation: cama_fix_filename basenames and strips non-word characters from the uploaded filename (lib/ext/string.rb:105-115; app/helpers/camaleon_cms/uploader_helper.rb:47-51).

Private-download existence gate: fetch_file refuses to serve a name unless file_exists? says it exists, and the route requires a signed-in user (app/uploaders/camaleon_cms_uploader.rb:163-165; app/uploaders/camaleon_cms_local_uploader.rb:27-31; app/uploaders/camaleon_cms_aws_uploader.rb:38-44; app/controllers/camaleon_cms/admin/media_controller.rb:5,28-34).
Media-mutation authorization: new_folder/del_folder/del_file require the :manage, :media ability; crop_url is explicitly exempt (app/controllers/camaleon_cms/admin/media_controller.rb:11,52).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The reported bug was an arbitrary path write through the upload folder; this is a download route behind a sign-in, and S3 object keys are opaque, so a '..' key cannot escape the bucket and download_file is only reached when no local file exists.
The advisory names the S3 implementation, while this is the default local uploader; the route is under the admin namespace and only checks file existence before send_file.

All three actions require :manage, :media, and the AWS implementation (the one the advisory names) already normalizes the same keys with cama_fix_media_key, so the local uploader looks like an out-of-scope admin feature.
The data: branch is fed from crop_url, whose action runs UserUrlValidator first, and the name parameter is not the folder the advisory names; it also needs a signed-in user.

params[:file_upload] is expected to be an UploadedFile; a plain String is the uploader's documented internal temp-file API that crop and cama_tmp_upload rely on, it is a read rather than the reported write, and the upload action requires a signed-in user.

conflicts.what: The natural containment guard for the private-download path is the existing valid_folder_path? rule, which rejects absolute paths (app/uploaders/camaleon_cms_uploader.rb:129); applied to upload_file's String input it also rejects the absolute public/tmp paths that the legitimate crop and crop_url flows hand back (app/controllers/camaleon_cms/admin/media_controller.rb:22,76; app/helpers/camaleon_cms/uploader_helper.rb:256,298), which T5's must-keep-working value needs.

Reusing valid_folder_path? for T3's params[:folder] rejects the leading-'/' keys the media UI sends for root items (app/assets/javascripts/camaleon_cms/admin/uploader/_media_manager.js:308,340; lib/ext/string.rb:100), while T1's private-download keys are generated with the leading slash stripped (app/uploaders/camaleon_cms_local_uploader.rb:62), so one string rule cannot serve both without normalization.

fairness_risks: Root-level media keys legitimately start with '/' (cama_fix_media_key forces a leading slash, lib/ext/string.rb:100-101; local file_parse builds keys from it, app/uploaders/camaleon_cms_local_uploader.rb:59; the UI posts data-folder + '/' + data-key, app/assets/javascripts/camaleon_cms/admin/uploader/_media_manager.js:308,340), so a valid_folder_path?-style absolute-path rejection on params[:folder] would break new_folder and del_file at the media root.

cama_fix_filename permits consecutive dots (sanitize_regexp /[^[:word:].\-+]/, lib/ext/string.rb:108), so a legitimate name such as 'v1..v2.png' would be refused by a blanket path.include?('..') rule applied to media keys used by delete_file/delete_folder.

upload_file is documented and used with absolute String paths: cama_tmp_upload returns File.join(Rails.public_path, 'tmp', site id, name) (app/helpers/camaleon_cms/uploader_helper.rb:256,298-301) and crop/crop_url pass it back (app/controllers/camaleon_cms/admin/media_controller.rb:22,76). Refusing absolute or String inputs to close T5 breaks the crop and remote-URL upload flows; the guard must allow the tmp root.

Private thumbnail URLs are generated keys containing slashes and dots (version_path(key).slice(1..-1) at app/uploaders/camaleon_cms_local_uploader.rb:62 and app/views/camaleon_cms/admin/media/_render_file_item.html.erb:18), so a basename-only rule on params[:file] would break private thumbnails.

design.why: The proposal has three independent fix sites with different dismissals. Group T1+T2 is the advisory sink itself: download_private_file feeds params[:file] straight into fetch_file in both uploaders, so one controller-side (or shared) containment guard closes both, yet the solver must notice the local twin that an S3-titled report does not name; the easy dismissal is 'this is a read behind sign-in and S3 keys are opaque'. T3 is the same missing key normalization in the local uploader's add_folder/delete_folder/delete_file, which the earlier fix applied only to the AWS path, dismissed because the actions require :manage, :media. T5 is upload_file's String-path branch, which is simultaneously the documented internal temp-file API used by crop and crop_url, so a blanket containment fix over-hardens and breaks legitimate flows (a coupled must-keep-working value). DeepSeek is exposed by the absent-protection-plus-dismissal sites (T3, T5); MiMo is exposed by the two-implementation how-type site (T1+T2) and by the coupled temp-path value (T5). T4 (cama_tmp_upload name write) would be a fourth independent write trap only if the data: path can pass UserUrlValidator, which the code suggests it cannot, so it is not part of the recommended design.
